steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React and useState into your component file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. These are essential for building accessible React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct import syntax.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty React fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to return the fragment.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns an empty React fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and return statement.

steps.title: Initialize state for accessibility mode
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a state variable called 'isAccessibilityMode' using useState, with a default value of false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should be a boolean that tracks whether accessibility features are enabled.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a boolean state variable
const [isDarkMode, setIsDarkMode] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a state variable 'isAccessibilityMode' initialized to false, ready to toggle accessibility features.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable declaration: const [isAccessibilityMode, setIsAccessibilityMode] = useState(false);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the accessibility mode state. This boolean will control whether accessibility enhancements are visible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with the exact variable name 'isAccessibilityMode' and defaulting it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use useState to create a state variable named 'isAccessibilityMode' with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Define toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, define a function called 'toggleAccessibilityMode' that toggles the 'isAccessibilityMode' state value.
steps.hint: Use the setter function from useState to update the state by toggling its boolean value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleAccessibilityMode function is defined and uses setIsAccessibilityMode to toggle the boolean state.
successCriteria: A function named toggleAccessibilityMode is defined inside the App component and toggles the isAccessibilityMode state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the toggle handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named toggleAccessibilityMode and properly toggles the state value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler function is not defined correctly. Check the function name and toggle logic.

steps.title: Add main container with semantic HTML
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your App component, replace the current `null` with a `<main>` element that contains a `<section>` element inside it.
steps.hint: The `<main>` element should be the top-level wrapper. Inside it, add a `<section>` element. You can leave the section empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a semantic HTML structure with `<main>` and `<section>` elements instead of `null`.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a `<main>` element wrapping a `<section>` element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the semantic HTML structure. Using `<main>` and `<section>` helps screen readers understand the page layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both a `<main>` element and a `<section>` element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced `null` with a `<main>` element containing a `<section>` element.

steps.title: Add heading with proper hierarchy
steps.instruction: Inside the main container section, add an h1 heading with the text 'Accessibility Demo'.
steps.hint: Use the <h1> element with the text content 'Accessibility Demo'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a main heading

Welcome to the App
steps.expectedOutcome: The main container section now contains an h1 heading with proper semantic hierarchy.
successCriteria: An h1 element with the text 'Accessibility Demo' is present inside the section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a proper h1 heading, which provides clear structure for screen readers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an h1 element with the exact text 'Accessibility Demo' inside the section.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading is missing or incorrect. Add an h1 element with the text 'Accessibility Demo' inside the section.

steps.title: Add descriptive paragraph text
steps.instruction: Inside the section element, add a paragraph element with descriptive text about accessibility.
steps.hint:
Use the

tag to create a paragraph. Write a sentence explaining why accessibility matters in web development.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a paragraph with meaningful content

This is an important message about web standards.
steps.expectedOutcome: The section element now contains a paragraph with descriptive accessibility text.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with descriptive text about accessibility is added inside the section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added meaningful content using a semantic paragraph element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a paragraph element with descriptive text about accessibility.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element with descriptive accessibility text is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add toggle button with accessibility attributes
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls toggleAccessibilityMode, an aria-label describing its purpose, and dynamic text that changes based on isAccessibilityMode state.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute to call your toggle function, set aria-label to something like 'Toggle accessibility mode', and use a ternary operator for the button text.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that toggles accessibility mode when clicked, has proper accessibility attributes, and displays appropriate text based on the current state.
successCriteria: Button element with onClick handler calling toggleAccessibilityMode, aria-label attribute, and dynamic text using isAccessibilityMode state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created an accessible button with proper event handling and ARIA attributes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your button has all three required elements: onClick handler, aria-label, and dynamic text based on state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing required accessibility features. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Add image with alt text
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an img element with a descriptive alt attribute that explains the image content.
steps.hint: Use the img tag with src and alt attributes. The alt text should describe what the image shows for screen readers.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding an accessible image
steps.expectedOutcome: An img element with src and alt attributes will be added to demonstrate proper image accessibility.
successCriteria: The code includes an img element with both src and alt attributes containing descriptive text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an accessible image with proper alt text that describes the image content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an image, but make sure it includes both src and alt attributes with descriptive text.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding an img element with src and alt attributes inside your component's return statement.

steps.title: Apply conditional styling based on accessibility mode
steps.instruction: Add a conditional className to the main <section> container that applies 'high-contrast' styles when accessibility mode is enabled.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally set the className attribute based on the isAccessibilityMode state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main container should have a conditional className that applies accessibility styles when the mode is active.
successCriteria: The <section> element has a className attribute
The className uses a ternary operator with isAccessibilityMode
The 'high-contrast' class is applied when isAccessibilityMode is true
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional styling that will improve readability for users with accessibility needs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the className attribute uses the isAccessibilityMode state in a ternary operator to conditionally apply the 'high-contrast' class.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a className attribute to the <section> element that conditionally applies 'high-contrast' based on the isAccessibilityMode state.
